newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman, Iran agree on ways of developing gas field.
newsitem.headline: Oman, Iran agree on ways of developing gas field.

text.p: Oman and Iran agreed on Sunday on ways of developing their shared offshore Henjam gas and condensate field in the Strait of Hormuz.

Salem bin Mohammad bin Sha'baan, undersecretary at Oman's oil ministry, told reporters after holding talks with an Iranian oil delegation in Muscat, that the two countries agreed on operational and legal guidelines for developing the field.
"Today there was an agreement on the principles on which the development of the field will be based on," he said.
He added that within two weeks a joint team would be formed to discuss financial and legal aspects of their agreement.
Henjam straddles the maritime border between the two oil producers and Iranian officials have estimated the field's gas reserves at one trillion cubic feet (30 billion cubic metres).
Gas and condensate is already produced from the Omani side of the shared field -- where it is known as the Bukha field -- and exports are sent by pipeline to the United Arab Emirates.
Analysts have estimated that the full development of the field will take about three years.
Sha'baan said Oman had drilled two exploratory wells on its side of the field and Iran had drilled one on its side.
The two countries set up a joint ministerial committee to study the field's development in 1990 and agreed in 1995 to jointly develop the field.
Oman and Iran in January agreed in principle to select firms to develop the joint field.
Henjam was first discovered in 1976 and Bukha in 1979.
